# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. This file is
the agent ENTRY document: the harness merges it into the system prompt with
a ~19 KB entry budget, so it must stay small enough to be fully visible.
Ceiling: **≤ 300 lines / ≤ 20 KB** — enforced by
`scripts/check_agents_md_size.sh` (pre-commit hook via `ci_fast_gate.sh` +
the CI `static` job). Subsystem essays live in `docs/` — index:
`docs/README.md`. Keep entries factual: paths, commands, invariants.

## Module map

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph CORE["SDK - flutter_agent_harness, pure Dart (lib/)"]
        AI["ai: providers, agent loop, sessions, compaction"]
        TOLS["tools: approval, redact, hashline, memory"]
        HOSTS["hosts: shared wiring, messaging, a2a, hub"]
    end
    subgraph PKG["packages/ - sibling Dart packages"]
        FAUI["fa_ui: widgets incl. trajectory"]
        DAP["dap_hub, fa_llm, fa_llm_mock"]
    end
    CLI["fa CLI - bin/ + lib/src/cli: TUI, slash commands, headless"]
    APP["Flutter app - flutter_app/: desktop, mobile, web shells"]
    EXT["Browser extension - browser_ext/ + lib/src/browser + serve_bridge"]
    OFFICE["Office add-in - office_addin/ + FA_HOST=office host"]
    GOLDEN["UI golden & styles - golden tests, themes, ui tests"]
    NETW["fa_network - external Go backend + network clients"]
    CORE --> CLI
    CORE --> APP
    CORE --> EXT
    PKG --> APP
    PKG --> CLI
    APP --> OFFICE
    CLI --> NETW
    APP --> NETW
    EXT --> NETW
    GOLDEN --> APP
    GOLDEN --> FAUI
```

## Project layout — one line per subsystem

Full subsystem reference: `docs/agents/sdk-subsystems.md` (SDK) +
`docs/agents/flutter-app-subsystems.md` (app/packages/repo-level).

**SDK core (`lib/`, pure Dart):**

- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers, session modes, per-tool overrides, critical-bash interceptor, per-turn grants.
- `lib/src/tools/` — `ask`/`request_secret`/media tools, `read` selectors + archives + sqlite, background shell jobs, availability + load modes.
- `lib/src/env/` — `ExecutionEnv` impls: `LocalShell` (setsid, killTree, drain caps, self-signal immunity), session-correlation vars, in-memory default.
- `lib/src/agent/` — FinalizeGate, tool pairing, session image registry.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — trajectory ledger core; goldens under `test/trajectory/goldens/`.
- `lib/src/redact/` — layered secret redaction (prompt, tool args, output, logs).
- `lib/src/hashline/` — `[path#TAG]` patch language (SWAP/DEL/INS, stale-tag rejection).
- `lib/src/compaction/` — branch summarization + AutoCompactor → policy: `docs/compaction.md`.
- `lib/src/lsp/`, `lib/src/mcp/` — `lsp` + MCP protocol tooling (lazy servers, pure-Dart transports).
- `lib/src/model_roles/` — roles/fallbacks/keyring/watchdogs + provider catalog; `lib/src/ttsr/` — streaming-interrupt rules.
- `lib/src/skills/`, `lib/src/prompts/` — skills discovery; AGENTS/CLAUDE/GOAL/DESIGN auto-merge into the system prompt.
- `lib/src/task/`, `lib/src/messaging/`, `lib/src/session/attach/` — subagents, inbox fabric, attached sessions → `docs/subagents/README.md`.
- `lib/src/memory/` — long-term memory (hosted `flutter_agent_memory` package) → pitfalls: `docs/memory-churn.md`.
- `lib/src/a2a/` — Agent2Agent client/server/manager (`fa serve --a2a`).
- `bin/fah.dart` + `lib/src/cli/` — the `fa` CLI: REPL, slash commands, headless/serve modes → `docs/agents/cli.md`.
- `lib/src/cube/` — fa_cube sandbox profiles → `docs/cubes.md`; `lib/src/cli/hep.dart` — HEP event protocol → `docs/hep.md`.

## Hard architecture rules (stay inline)

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.
- Barrel `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart`: grouped **APPEND-ONLY** export
  sections — one `// ── <subsystem> ──` header per group, sorted by path
  within a group, new exports append to their group. No mini-barrels, no
  re-sorting (gh-1232).
- God-file ceiling: no `.dart` file over **2800** lines (crap4dart `loc`
  gate). Target < 2000 for primary files; split by concern into `part`
  files — never by extracting public API.

## Working in parallel (shared checkout + worktrees)

Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked; run no
heavy commands (full suites/analyze) in it; never `git stash` the user's
WIP; talk to peer agents through the messaging fabric, not their files.

`.worktrees/<name>/` from the remote tracking ref, remove when done.

then `memory_list` for fuzzy topics). Scopes: **project** = this repo

user's files: read freely, write only via `memory_add`), **user** = global/private. `memory_add` stores durable facts

+// CI-authentic zips in ~/vendor-cache/ on the runner box (launchd
+// refresher). These asserts pin how the workflows consume that cache
+// WITHOUT breaking the incident guards that predate it:

+//   gh-2233 (wasmrun_restore_temp_race_test): the arch-less shared
+//     /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip path must not appear ANYWHERE in the
+//     iOS step — so the seed source is ONLY ~/vendor-cache/, never /tmp.
+//   gh-1759 (wasmrun_restore_budget_test): build-macos.yml must not
+//     contain `rm -f "$ZIP"` before the download loop, and its first
+//     occurrence must be the post-loop self-heal purge — so the seed
+//     verifies a CANDIDATE file and only `mv`s it onto "$ZIP" when the
+//     pinned sha256 matches; a bad candidate is discarded by its own
+//     name, never by touching the partial.
+//

+//        the candidate+mv pattern, before the digest-valid skip.
+//   AC2  iOS keeps $RUNNER_TEMP as the only download target.
+//   AC3  macOS keeps per-arch /tmp partials and seeds cold ones from
+//        ~/vendor-cache/$(basename "$ZIP") via the same candidate+mv

_Previous review discussions for PR #2295._

> ℹ️ **2 resolved thread(s) excluded; 7 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

**ai-teammate** (2026-11-18):

🚨 severity: BLOCKING —
🚨 **BLOCKING: `$TMP` is expanded before it is assigned — the WWDR import branch crashes `ci-sign install` outright on its first real run**

`scripts/ci-sign` runs under `set -euo pipefail` (`scripts/ci-sign:58`), but this new block sits **before** `TMP="$(mktemp -d)"` (`scripts/ci-sign:287`). At line 283, `"$TMP/wwdr.pem"` expands while `TMP` is still unset, so the first time the guard actually triggers — a keychain with no WWDR certificate, i.e. exactly the first run this PR targets — bash aborts before `curl` even starts:

```
scripts/ci-sign: line 283: TMP: unbound variable   (exit 1)
```

Verified by reproducing the exact control flow (`if ! <guard fails>; then curl -fsSL "$URL" -o "$TMP/wwdr.pem"; fi` under `set -euo pipefail` → aborts with "TMP: unbound variable"; assigning `TMP` before the block → proceeds).

Consequences:

- The WWDR G6 import can **never** succeed through this script — the guard keeps missing, so the crash repeats on every `install` until someone imports the cert manually. The feature is dead on arrival.
- Every `ci-sign install` on a host without the cert dies — including the per-build re-verification installs in `build-macos.yml:587/1016/1150`, `build-mobile.yml:1162`, and `host-signing-provision.yml` — a full signing outage on the pool.
- `install <label> --force` (the documented recovery path) is bricked: it deletes the keychain (`scripts/ci-sign:271`), `ensure_keychain` recreates it empty, the guard triggers → crash.

Static gates stay green, which is why the PR's verification (bash -n clean) missed it: `bash -n` is syntax-only, and ShellCheck raises no SC2154 because `TMP` *does* get assigned later in the same case block. Only a runtime `set -u` trip exposes it.

**Fix**: move the whole block below `TMP="$(mktemp -d)"` and the consolidated EXIT trap (`scripts/ci-sign:287-290`). That also gives `wwdr.pem` EXIT cleanup for free — at its current position even a working download would escape the `rm -rf "$TMP"` cleanup.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-11-18):

⚠️ severity: IMPORTANT —
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the idempotency guard matches ANY "Apple Worldwide Developer Relations" certificate — an older or expired generation permanently suppresses the G6 import**

`security find-certificate -a -c` matches on the certificate's name attribute as an unanchored regex and does not consider validity. Every WWDR intermediate generation shares the same CN ("Apple Worldwide Developer Relations Certification Authority"), so a single G3/G4/G5 intermediate — including a long-expired one — in this keychain makes the guard succeed and the G6 import is silently skipped forever.

That is not hypothetical for *this* keychain: the same script documents the mechanism (`scripts/ci-sign:311`, gh-2008 note): *"Xcode's export -allowProvisioningUpdates silently imports Apple-issued certs into the persistent keychain"*. P12 imports can carry the export-time chain as well. Whatever generation those paths bring in is not necessarily G6 — and the failure mode is silent: codesign verification chains that need G6 start failing with "unable to build chain", exactly the class of breakage this PR exists to prevent. On a fresh empty keychain the guard behaves correctly, which is why this is not a BLOCKING.

**Fix**: guard on the specific certificate, not the shared CN substring — compare the Apple-published G6 SHA-1/serial (e.g. dump `security find-certificate -a -p "$KC"` PEM and match the fingerprint, or match the hash attribute in `find-certificate` output) before skipping the import.

arguments.content:
💡 **SUGGESTION: `grep -qi` + `set -o pipefail` — SIGPIPE race can flip the G6 presence guard to false-negative**

The guard pipeline:

```bash
if ! security find-certificate -a -Z -c "Apple Worldwide Developer Relations" "$KC" 2>/dev/null \
    | tr -d ' :' | grep -qi "$WWDR_G6_SHA1"; then
```

`grep -q` exits at the **first** match. If at that moment `security`/`tr` still have output to write (the `-Z` listing spans multiple pipe writes and the G6 match lands in an early block), `tr`'s next write raises SIGPIPE and the pipeline's status becomes non-zero (`tr` exit 141) **even though grep matched** — `set -o pipefail` (line 58) propagates the leftmost non-zero status. Inside `if !`, that non-zero status reads as "G6 absent", so the branch re-downloads and re-imports a certificate that is already present; `security import` then fails as a duplicate and emits the WARN `"WWDR G6 import failed — codesign chains may not verify"` — a false alarm on every affected run.

Runtime-verified with the exact pipeline shape under `set -euo pipefail`, G6 match emitted first followed by ~110 KB of further WWDR blocks: `GUARD-MISS -> import branch` on repeated runs, with `echo: write error: Broken pipe` from the producer.

**Why suggestion, not important**: real keychains carry only a handful of WWDR intermediates, so the `-Z` output is ~2 KB — far below the 64 KB pipe buffer, meaning `tr` almost always completes all writes in a single round before `grep` exits. The latent consequence is bounded (one redundant fetch + a spurious WARN; the keychain keeps its G6; `install` proceeds) — no signing breakage, no state corruption. If this pool ever accumulates a large WWDR-matching cert set, the false-WARN noise would justify raising this to ⚠️.

**Fix** (one word): drop `-q` — `grep -i "$WWDR_G6_SHA1"` reads to EOF, so `tr` never SIGPIPEs and pipefail sees 0 on a match; the stream is tiny, so draining costs nothing:

```bash
if ! security find-certificate -a -Z -c "Apple Worldwide Developer Relations" "$KC" 2>/dev/null \
    | tr -d ' :' | grep -i "$WWDR_G6_SHA1" >/dev/null; then
```
